Finally, Combined with the KNN idea, we find the k complete data that are most similar to each missing data, use information entropy to calculate the weight coefficients of the k complete data, and weight the corresponding attributes of the complete data to fill in the missing attributes. Experimental results show that the data filling algorithm in this paper has better filling precision than k-means and KNN algorithms.

articleTitle: Joint Sparse Channel Estimation Under NOMA Scheme for Many Access MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing orthogonal multiple access methods can not accommodate the number of devices required in the 5G era. Active device detection combined with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) solution can accommodate more devices. The impact of the NOMA scheme on the performance of active device detection, channel estimation, and decoding has been analyzed. Theoretical and simulation results show that: With the addition of the NOMA scheme, the active device detection performance will decrease slightly, but it will greatly improve the decoding performance and system capacity. Simulation and theoretical results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: CRC-Polar Codes in TRPC-UWB Communication System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Transmitted reference pulse cluster (TRPC) signaling structure was proposed to overcome long wideband delay line requirement of conventional transmitted reference (TR-) ultra-wideband (UWB) system. In uncoded cases, it has been demonstrated that the bit error rate (BER) performance of TRPC-UWB system significantly outperforms the conventional TR-UWB system, BER is the number of error bits divided by the total number of transmitted bits during a study interval. In order to further improve the BER performance of TRPC-UWB system, different forward error correction (FEC) codes were investigated, such as Reed-Solomon (RS) codes, convolutional codes, low density parity check (LDPC) codes and polar codes. This paper introduces the cyclic redundancy check (CRC-) to polar coded TRPC-UWB system to improve the coding gain of polar codes in the TRPC-UWB system. The effect of different CRC codes on the performance of CRC-polar coded TRPC-UWB system is evaluated and the performance comparisons between CRC-polar codes and other FEC codes are provided. Simulation results show that appropriate selection of decoding paths and CRC bits can effectively improve the BER performance of TRPC-UWB system.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Accelerator for Independently Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recurrent neural network has been widely used in the field of machine learning, especially in addressing sequence learning problems. However, normal RNN and its variants LSTM and GRU, are fully connected networks which require a large number of parameters for calculation. For an FPGA accelerator, these neural networks usually consume a lot of energy for calculation and require a lot of memory access. Recent theory has shown that an independently recurrent neural network (IndRNN) can reduce memory access and calculation consumption with negligible accuracy loss, which make RNN easy to be deployed on an FPGA board. This paper implements this approach on a Xilinx Zynq zc706 FPGA and focuses on improving the efficiency of the network, including energy, resources and throughput. This accelerator uses massively parallel processing elements (PEs) for low latency and high throughput. The weights are stored in on-chip memory for low bandwidth requirement and less memory access. FPGA experimental results from a 2 layers IndRNN with 128 hidden units in each layer show that the accelerator uses less on-chip resources but can achieve better performance.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Improved Progressive Bit-Flipping Decoding for Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The decoding performance of successive cancellation (SC) can be improved by correcting the error bits caused by channel noises. In order to identify and correct those error bits, we propose an improved progressive bit-flipping (IPBF) decoding algorithm. First, a more efficient method of constructing the set of error bit positions (EBPs) is proposed. It can significantly reduce the size of the set of EBPs, especially at medium to high signal to noise ratio (SNR). Second, a pruning technique of reducing the number of error bit-flipping combinations (EBFCs) is presented. In the case of ensuring that the decoding performance of PBF algorithm is not degraded, the decoding complexity is reduced as much as possible with the help of the pruning scheme. From the simulation results, compared to the conventional PBF algorithm, the proposed IPBF algorithm not only significantly reduces the average decoding complexity, but also has a slight improvement in decoding performance. At 2.0dB, the decoding complexity can be reduced by 63.6%, 87.5%, and 97.6% when ω is equal to 2, 3 and 4, respectively.

articleTitle: End-to-End Chinese Dialect Identification Using Deep Feature Model of Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: End-to-end Chinese dialect identification (DID) system based on Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) has been proposed in recent years. However, most neural DID methods overlook the using of deep feature of speech, although deep feature has been used successfully in conventional DID systems. This paper proposes using 1-Dimension (1-D) CNN to extract deep feature of speech, at the same time, this paper also focuses on extracting time information of speech for end-to-end DID in RNN. Our experiments conducted on the Chinese dialect voice data set from IFLYTEK, provided the method of generative auditory model using 1-D CNN simulation is very effective. 1-D CNN simulates the filtering operations by the cochlea, and fully utilizes the information mining and classification processing ability of the CNN. In the training process, the accuracy rate by the method proposed in this paper is 5.9% higher than early acoustic neural methods.

articleTitle: Research on Chinese Named Entity Recognition Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Named entity recognition is a fundamental and important task in the field of natural language processing. The effect of existing solutions in practical applications do not meet need of people. Firstly, this paper studies the scheme of recurrent neural networks with conditional random fields. Further, a series of experiments were performed on the input word vector dimension, the number of neural nodes within the neural network, and the variant structure of neural networks. Finally, a method of combining neural network with attention mechanism is proposed. An attention layer is built over the output of the recurrent neural network and the F1 score reaches 91.28%.

articleTitle: Road-Map Aided VSIMM-GMPHD Filter for Ground Moving Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Tracking multiple ground moving targets with uncertain target dynamics proves to be a complicated task, especially when the number of targets varies. This paper presents a road-map aided variable structure interacting multiple model Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density (RA-VSIMM-GMPHD) filter for ground moving targets tracking using moving target detector (MTD) measurements obtained from a monostatic radar. The probability hypothesis density (PHD) filter, which is a recursive Bayesian algorithm for jointly estimating the time-varying number of targets and their states in clutter, has been shown to be a computationally efficient solution to multi-target tracking problems with a varying number of targets. Specifically, the Gaussian mixture PHD (GMPHD) is a closed-form solution to the PHD recursion under linear, Gaussian assumptions on the target dynamics. The target dynamics uncertainty can be resolved by road-map aided variable structure interacting multiple model (VSIMM) estimator, in which the mode sets are modified adaptively depending on the road-map. The RA-VSIMM-GMPHD filter, which incorporates road-map aided VSIMM estimator into a framework of GMPHD filter, is particularly suited to tracking ground moving targets with uncertain dynamics and number varies. Simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed filter over single-model GMPHD filter and VSIMM estimator.

articleTitle: Road Map Extraction Using GMPHD Filter and Linear Regression Method for Ground Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The effective use of road map information can greatly improve the ground target tracking performance, but in the cases where the road map is not available, the road map can be extracted through the target state moving on the road. Therefore, this paper has proposed a novel road map extraction algorithm in the Random Finite Set (RFS) formulation. This novel algorithm exploits the Gaussian Mixture Probability Hypothesis Density (GMPHD) filter and linear regression method to extract the road map. First of all, the single target state is estimated by the GMPHD filter in clutter, and the estimation of multiple-target state in continuous observation time constitutes the historical data of multi-target state. Then, the linear regression method is performed on these data. The linear model is the road model, and the training set is the historical data of multi-target state. After the above two steps, the road map can be extracted. The performance of the proposed algorithm is validated through the road map extraction simulation. The simulation results demonstrate that compared with the existing methods, the precision of the extracted road segment can be improved significantly through the proposed algorithm. Further, the extracted road is used for the ground target tracking. The simulation results indicate that the road information extracted by the algorithm proposed in this paper can effectively improve the tracking precision of moving targets on the road.

Author Keywords: gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filter

articleTitle: Enterprise Lean Catering Material Management Information System Based on Sequence Pattern Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Data mining technology is used to solve the problems of inventory purchasing warning, fine preparation, freshness warning and performance appraisal on the basis of the traditional enterprise catering material management system. Using sequence pattern data mining technology to support the level of food and beverage management effectively, it has a great significance for enterprises to reduce cost and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Efficient Bandwidth Management (EBM) Algorithm for NG-EPON
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Next generation Ethernet passive optical network (NG-EPON) is a promising technology to cater the huge bandwidth and efficient distribution demands of the future Internet. An important task in NG-EPON is designing of dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA) algorithms. A number of DBA algorithms proposed for TWDM EPON could be used for NG-EPON by making suitable parametric changes. However, new DBA algorithms for a class of NG-EPON called MSD EPON are required to proficiently meet the bandwidth demands of NG-EPON. In this paper, a new DBA algorithm for NG-EPON is reported. Proposed algorithm has been compared with the existing algorithms like earlier finished time (EFT) and earlier finished time with void filling (EFT-VF). Simulation results show that our DBA algorithm performs better in terms of important performance measures like average packet delay and average completion time.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Classification for Driving Scenarios Based on Big Data and Ontology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent connected vehicle technology, the construction of driving scenarios library has become more urgent and important, and its completeness directly determines the perception and decision-making ability of intelligent connected vehicles. To solve the problem of high cost and insufficient coverage for driving scenarios data collection, this research proposes a driving scenarios modeling and automatic classification algorithm based on big data and ontology. Specifically, the driving scenarios are first modeled based on ontology, and the data from multiple sensors are fused to instantiate the driving scenarios model. Furthermore, the scenarios rule base is constructed based on the expert experience and laws. Finally, combining the scenarios rule base and the instantiated scenarios, the inference engine is used to realize the automatic classification of driving scenarios, which provides the basis for further building a more complete driving scenarios library.

articleTitle: Seismic Signal Detection Algorithm Based on GS Transform Filtering and EMD Denoising
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A seismic detection algorithm based on Generalized S-transform (GS) filtering and Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) denoising is proposed in this paper. The algorithm is compared with the traditional method which using the energy ratio method (STA/LTA) after a single filtering, it can effective improve the detection characteristic value of seismic signal in the case of low signal-to-noise ratio, so as to improve the detection probability of the signal effectively. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the detection eigenvalue of seismic signals when using the low signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Beam Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Liquid Crystal Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A novel design method of electronically controlled beam reconfigurable antenna using liquid crystal metasurface is presented in this paper. The metasurface is a two-dimensional plane composed of a series of sub-wavelength liquid crystal unit cells. The beam in desired radiation direction can be achieved by varying the impedance distribution of liquid crystal metasurface according to microwave holographic technique. In the simulation, we can obtain an arbitrary radiation direction beam within the zenith angle range of 35°~60° at 39 GHz, and the maximum gain reaches 10.65 dB. Such a beam reconfigurable antenna with low profile ( 44 mm * 44 mm * 2.15 mm) and continuously adjustable beam has great value in practical applications of mobile communications.

articleTitle: EasiSMR: Recognizing Non-Specific Low Back Pain Symptomatic Muscles Using Multi-Muscles Fusion based Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Non-specific low back pain (NLBP) is a symptom of the unknown pathoanatomical cause. The treatment focuses on reducing pain and disability based on doctor's experiences, which is usually with the insufficient support of objective evidence. Helping doctors recognize symptomatic muscles and giving patients more precise treatment accordingly are big practical challenges. Surface electromyography (sEMG) is the collective electric signal from muscles, which is a widely used and noninvasive way to have an insight into the muscles. With the rapid development of machine learning and signal processing in biomedical engineering, many problems requiring individual judgment can possibly be solved by building appropriate computing models based on the heterogeneous and complex dataset, as the approach we used to address the practical challenges. In this work, a novel NLBP Symptomatic Muscles Recognition method (EasiSMR) is proposed to accurately locate the symptomatic muscles, and an objective evaluation is then provided based on wearable sEMG measurements. EasiSMR is designed to build machine learning models for six low back muscles separately which enables to recognize the symptomatic muscles via an isometric exercise. EasiSMR possesses two main contributions to enhance its recognition performance: a Multi-Muscles Fusion method (MMF) which takes the muscle compensation information into account, and a set of new features are extracted for isometric exercise which reflects the characteristics of muscle firing phase. Intensive experiments were carried out to verify the performance of EasiSMR on the real-world NLBP sEMG dataset collected in hospital. Results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average recognition accuracy of 86.16% for all six low back muscles and shows potential value in NLBP treatment.

articleTitle: Detecting Anomalies in Distributed Control Systems by Modeling Traffic Behaviors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Intrusion detection based on network traffic has been widely studied in traditional network systems. At the same time, the security threats faced by Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are becoming increasingly severe. The network communication environments of ICSs are very different from the traditional Internet in in terms of protocols, interaction modes and security considerations. How to detect anomalies effectively in power production control system is an important issue. In this work, we use a representative Distributed Control System (DCS) working in thermal power generation scenarios and conduct various attacks on this DCS to generate an original network traffic. We then consider the time correlation and interaction stability of the DCS and propose a dual window scheme (Dual-Win) to get more effective features based on basic features. We use several machine learning methods for the detection of anomalies based on the traffic data. The experimental results show that our method achieves the detection accuracy as 99.41% with only basic traffic features, and the detection accuracy can be as 99.77% with the basic and Dual-Win features.

articleTitle: Extended Generalised Spatial Modulation with Variable Number of Activated Transmit Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: An extended generalised spatial modulation (E-GSM) technique is proposed. Unlike the conventional spatial modulation (SM) schemes where the number of activated transmit antennas (TAs) has been fixed, the E-GSM scheme employs variable number of activated TAs to represent the explicit spatial symbol, which makes fuller use of the transmit antenna combinations (TACs) and thus, enhances the spectral efficiency. The average bit error ratio of the proposed E-GSM is derived in a closed-form expression and the theoretical analysis agrees well with the numerical results. In addition, to further improve the system performance, the optimal set of the TACs is derived based on the pairwise error probability. Simulation results demonstrate that the E-GSM scheme can achieve a higher spectral efficiency for a given number of TAs compared with existing transmit-side SM schemes. Moreover, it is shown that, for a fixed spectral efficiency, the E-GSM scheme outperforms the conventional SM schemes in terms of the error performance.

articleTitle: Human Classification Based on Micro-Doppler Features of Walking Using Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, a human classification method based on the convolution neural network (CNN) is proposed. The proposed method firstly applies the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to the radar received signal, which is denoised by the principal components analysis, to obtain the micro-Doppler spectrogram. Then, a new feature extraction scheme is proposed to extract 2-dimentional feature from the micro-Doppler spectrogram. Finally, we construct a CNN to realize the human classification. In order to validate the human classification method, training and testing data are produced by using a human walking model with linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) and the additive white Gaussian noise is added to the simulation data. Simulations are carried out under different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and the trained neural network can distinct 5 people with up to 100% of accuracy with high SNR. Simulation results verify the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Survey of Gene Selection and Classification Techniques Based on Cancer Microarray Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A growing number of cancer deaths draws attractions in the areas of bioinformatics worldwide. It is worth noting that cancer microarray data is composed of tens of thousands of genes, but there are only a few dozens of genes that are really relative to cancers. Thus, it is particularly import to pick out the relevant genes by means of microarray data analysis. Gene selection and classification techniques capture the essence of cancer mechanism and represent a suite of the refreshing cancer cure. In the paper, we summarize 4 types of cancer microarrays which show up in reference providing their attributes and download websites. Furthermore, we also review most extensively studied gene selection and classification techniques. Meanwhile, comparison and analysis on accuracies of gene selection and classification methods in view of remarkably influential algorithms are outlined with unique and randomized algorithms. Thus, the most correlative cancer genes are selected, Leukemia and Colon cancer as typical representatives are listed in the survey. From the microcosmic perspectives, these emerging techniques are considerably conductive to solve the dimensional curse of cancer microarray data applied in the treatment of cancer.

articleTitle: Fuzzy C-means Thresholding for a Brain MRI Image Based on Edge Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Fuzzy C-means thresholding with a Gaussian filter based on edge-detection technique is proposed to segment the cluster-edge-detection boundary in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). With an MRI scan as an input image, fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering is used to create image clusters, which show white and gray matter. In this process, 5% Gaussian blur noise is added to the image clusters. A Gaussian filter is used to remove or reduce the Gaussian blur noise. Canny edge-detection method was used for the edge detection of a boundary of cluster image after removing the blur noise. Then, the boundary of the cluster image is segmented and extracted by thresholding. The proposed method is successfully utilized to segment the boundary of cluster images. The method efficiently produces low mean-squared error (MSE) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) for a boundary of cluster images compared with previously reported methods.

articleTitle: Multiple Access Protocol for ad-hoc networks in VHF Data Exchange System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Very High Frequency (VHF) Data Exchange System (VDES) will provide enhanced data exchange capabilities for maritime VHF bands worldwide, supporting future e-Navigation and Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) modernization and protecting the current Automatic Identification System (AIS) system from heavy load. Based on the preliminary Recommendations for VDES, this paper focuses on the principle, process and algorithm implementation of Self-Organized Time Division Multiple Access (SOTDMA) channel access schemes for ad-hoc networks (ship-to-ship) in VDES, which is based on traditional TDMA and specified for marine scene. Furthermore, due to the self-organizing behavior of ad-hoc networks, slot reservation is not without potential conflicts, we thus analyze the collision probabilities of SOTDMA for two or more ships and their effects on the performance of ad-hoc networks in VDES.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging Algorithm of Maneuvering Target Based on Matching Flourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: When the maneuvering target is imaging in ISAR, the equivalent rotational speed of the target is non-uniform, and the cross-range compression by the Fourier transform will lead to defocusing of the image. In this paper, the matching Fourier transform is applied to the ISAR imaging of maneuvering target. The cross-range compression is completed by constructing a basis function that is consistent with the target cross-range phase, which eliminates the problem of image defocusing caused by the non-uniform target speed of rotation. Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Rate-adaptive Polar Codes Design for MLC NAND Flash Memory
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, rate-adaptive polar codes design based on memory cell bits' Bhattacharyya parameters to further improve the storage efficiency of multi-level cell (MLC) is proposed for NAND flash memory. The code design takes advantages of the inherent characteristics of MLC flash memory channel to iteratively calculate the bhattacharyya parameter of each memory cell bit, where the punctured positions are selected by choosing the bits with higher Bhattacharyya parameters to construct rate-adaptive polar codes. The experimental evaluations show that polar codes with code rate 0.8 punctured by the proposed method for MLC NAND flash memory channel can achieve 4.6 dB performance gain in bit error rate (BER) 8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> over the random puncturing codes.

articleTitle: The Impact of Bathtub Water Temperature on Personal Identification with ECG Signal based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper explores the impact of bathtub water temperature on personal identification with ECG signal using convolutional neural network. Ten volunteers' ECG records are collected with lead-III at low temperature of bathtub water (38±0.2 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> C in average) and high temperature of bathtub water (42±0.5 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C in average) environments, respectively. Each record is about 5±1 minutes at low temperature and 4±1 minutes at high temperature. In the data preprocessing stage, we denoise the original ECG signal and segment the QRS complex on a beat-by-beat basis. Then, we perform two interpolation calculations based on the QRS segmentation and convert the QRS complex into a binary image one by one. When we use the ECG signals which are collected at low temperature to train and test the CNN model, the identification rate is 82.67%. However, if we use the ECG signal collected at high temperature to test this trained CNN model, the identification rate is only 13.33%. Conversely, when we use the ECG signal collected at high temperature to train and test the CNN model, the identification rate is 85.50%. However, if we use the ECG signal collected at low temperature to test this trained CNN model, the identification rate is only 12.17%. Thus, we notice that the different bathtub water temperature has an important impact on the ECG signal patterns and it is feasible to perform personal identification by convolutional neural network with ECG signal collected during bathing at the same temperature.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Dual-Channel Structure for Software-Defined Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traditional software defined wireless sensor networks (SDWSN) fails to reduce the packet loss rate and delay due to the collision of packets in a single frequency channel. Considering a large network with numerous nodes, how to solve this issue becomes extremely essential. So, in this paper, we propose an SDWSN network architecture based on dual frequency channels (dual-channel structure), which enables topology control information and sensing data information to be transmitted in two independent frequency channels. To compare with single channel mode, we simulated the dual-channel structure based on the first order radio model. The numerical results show that the dual-channel structure has better performance on reducing network energy consumption and packet loss rate. The advantages of the dual-channel structure are also analyzed through hardware test. The test results show that the dual-channel structure is better than the traditional single channel structure in terms of node lifetime, delay and packet loss.

articleTitle: An Improved Algorithm for Multi-Swarm Particle Swarm Optimization Based on Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper studies the effects of logical random grouping and physical location grouping on the performance of multi-population particle swarm optimization (MSPSO) algorithm and realizes the dynamic grouping of multi-swarm particle optimization algorithms by introducing clustering algorithm. And the effects of K-Means algorithm, K-Medoids algorithm and DBSCAN algorithm on MSPSO are compared.

articleTitle: Locality-Aware PMI Usage for Efficient MPI Startup
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we examine usage of the Process Management Interface (PMI) during MPI_Init. Specifically, how PMI is used to exchange address information between peer processes in an MPI job. As node and core counts continue to increase in HPC systems, so does the amount of address data processes need to exchange. We show how by applying well-established locality-awareness techniques, we can significantly reduce the time spent in MPI_Init. We first present the use of shared memory to reduce the total amount of information retrieved from PMI. Next, by combining shared memory with a minimally connected set of processes, we further reduce the dependence on PMI, and employ the HPC fabric to transfer the bulk of address data. Our approach is low impact, relying on functionality already provided by MPI libraries and process managers, instead of new APIs and capabilities.

articleTitle: A Correlation-aware Diverse Variant Placement to Increase Network Resilience
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the high homogeneity of current routing infrastructure, the resilience of the network is facing a serious threat when a defective software upgrade or a denial-of-service attack occurs. Many existing works adopt heterogeneity philosophy to improve the resilience of the network. For example, diverse variants are placed to nodes in the network. However, the existing works assume that diverse variants do not have common vulnerabilities, which is an invalid assumption in some real networks. Therefore, the existing diverse variant placement algorithms could not achieve optimal performance. In this paper, we consider the situation that some variants have common vulnerabilities. We model the correlation-aware diverse variant placement problem as an integer-programming optimization problem. Since the problem is NP-hard, we design a Simulated Annealing-based algorithm to efficiently solve the problem. The simulation results show that compared with baseline algorithms, the proposed algorithms can effectively improve network resilience about 15%.

articleTitle: Image-Based Label Placement for Augmented Reality Browsers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a label placement technique for placing labels in Augmented Reality systems. One of the common challenges in Augmented Reality applications is lacking in knowledge of the real environment, limiting efficient representation and optimal layout of the digital information augment onto user's view. In order to overcome this problem, we propose an image-based label placement method, which combines identifying potentially important image regions and determining manual placement tendencies while labeling. Then we add geometric constraints for placing labels in the optimization problem to obtain the final label layout. Our method will provide special benefits to Augmented Reality browsers which is usually in the absence of scene knowledge. Also it can be used to many similar applications in the domain of Augmented Reality.

articleTitle: An Efficient Genetic Algorithm of Multi-Constellation Satellite Selection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Tracking enough visible GNSS satellites is becoming more and more significant, because of the growing demand of higher positioning precision. More and more satellites are launched, which is beneficial to positioning and causing huger tracking burden in the meantime. In this paper, we have integrated the genetic algorithm into multi-constellation GNSS satellites selection and analyzed its performance. Our efficient genetic algorithm of multi-constellation satellites (GPS, BeiDou, Galileo and Glonass) selection(EGAMS), whose parameters are determined by grid search method, will give the optimal satellite's combination candidates. The simulation results between EGAMS and traditional optimal satellite selection algorithm (TOSSA) indicate that EGAMS has a significant improvement on the computational complexity with the same accuracy according to WGDOP. In the meantime, the time consumption of EGAMS dramatically decreases 75% compared with TOSSA.

articleTitle: User Behavior Analyses in Mobile Personal Livecasts
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile communication technology, broadband wireless access technology, and mobile terminal technology, mobile personal livecasts have emerged and received extensive attention. In recent years, livecasting platforms have continuously increased in number, and they place a heavy emphasis on the measurement of video quality and customer satisfaction. We analyze user behaviors based on the CDN(Content Delivery Network) node log data from real CDN network environments of interactive livecasting platforms. Using the log information, the user behavior and habits of livecast viewers are analyzed according to geographical region and time period. Based on these user behaviors in different regions, resources are allocated differently at different time periods to optimize the CDN edge node server configuration. This allows the livecast system to provide better services with the same number of total CDN edge servers.

articleTitle: A Discretization Method for Floating-Point Number in FPGA-based Decision Tree Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Decision tree is one of the most popular supervised machine learning algorithms. Due to the rapid increase in the amount of data, many application scenarios require higher classification speed. Therefore, a variety of decision tree classification acceleration algorithms based on FPGA are proposed. These methods focus on improving the classification speed by designing effective pipeline architecture. However, the impact of floating-point numbers on storage and computing resources in the hardware implementation of the decision tree is ignored. In this paper, we present a discretization method for floating-point numbers in decision tree model by converting the floating-point numbers into integers. This method reduces the storage and computing resources required by the hardware implementation of decision tree, without affecting the classification performance of the classifier.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Biconical Antenna with Asymmetric Configuration
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a compact and miniaturized biconical antenna with an asymmetric configuration. Firstly, several vital parameters which affect the performance of biconical antenna were introduced concisely. Then the basic model of biconical antenna was constructed, and the model was illustrated briefly. Finally, the simulation process was carried out with ANSOFT HFSS 15.0 by changing the flare angle of the biconical antenna. As a result, an asymmetric biconical antenna with the impedance bandwidth of 3.1GHz-10.6GHz was designed. Within this operating frequency, the antenna has an omnidirectional radiation pattern, the voltage standing wave ratio (VWRS) is less than 1.8, the return loss (S11) is less than 10.5dB, and the average gain can reach more than 5dBi, the comprehensive performance is relatively better than classic biconical antenna, it can effectively satisfies the basic requirements of antenna communication system.

articleTitle: Unequal Clustering and Routing Algorithm Based on Dynamic Topology for WSN
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: For a large-scale wireless sensor networks (WSN), multi-hop communication will cause “energy holes” phenomenon. In order to improve the stability of WSN performance and balance the overall network load, a dynamic unequal clustering and routing algorithm for WSN (DUCR) is proposed in this paper. First, an unequal clustering algorithm is put forward based on WSN dynamic topology. Second, a WSN routing algorithm based on dynamic unequal clustering with fault tolerance mechanism is proposed to maximize parallel transmission. In the dynamic CH rotation phase, the base station is notified to re-clustering only when the number of cluster members is beyond the threshold, thereby adapting to the dynamic topology while reducing the overhead of frequent clustering. Extensive simulation experiments show that the DUCR can balance the network load, improve the stability of WSN performance and prolong the network lifetime.

articleTitle: A Checkerboard Corner Detection Method Using Circular Samplers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The accuracy of camera calibration depends a large extent on the corner detection accuracy. Thus, the checkerboard corner detection plays a fundamental role in the checkerboard based camera calibration. In this paper, we present a checkerboard corner detection method utilizing the specific frequency amplitudes of the boundary sequence at the checkerboard corner, which involves a coarse-to-fine strategy. The sub-pixel coordinates of corners are also calculated for higher accuracy. Experiment results with real images show that the method is capable of achieving high detection accuracy, hence providing reliable preprocessed data for high resolution camera calibration.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Application of Short Wave Transmitter Based on Stacked Auto-Encoder
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traditional methods for fault diagnosis of transmitters are mainly based on expert systems. This method requires manual extraction of data features, which is inevitably affected by human factors, and is prone to diagnostic errors. Aimed at this problem, this paper proposes deep learning theory to extract the deep feature representation of fault information, and construct a fault diagnosis model based on Stacked Auto-Encoder. Firstly, the collected fault signals are normalized, and the network is trained layer by layer using classless data. Then the network parameters are fine-tuned according to the tagged fault data, the fault signal features are automatically extracted. Finally, the trained network is used to detect various fault signals. Through simulation analysis, this method effectively reduces the diagnostic error, and the diagnostic performance is superior to the traditional diagnostic methods.

articleTitle: A Robust Fractal Tag Antenna for UHF RFID
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To improve the robustness of the RFID tag antenna for consumer-level application, this paper presents a UHF RFID antenna based on the characteristics of the tree-liked fractal. The paper exhibits a broad bandwidth with a resonance frequency locating at 900 MHz and the -10dB relative impedance bandwidth is 25% (630MHz-1050MHz). The radiation of the antenna is also pretty good with omnidirectional and a maximum gain of 3.24 dBi on its boresight. More importantly, the proposed antenna can maintain the good matching and radiation performance even large areas of the antenna surface are cut out, which cannot be achieved in other RFID tag antennas such as the commonly used ALN-9640 and ALN-9654 RFID tag antennas. The fractal RFID antenna proposed in this paper outperforms other tag antennas on injury resist. This capability enables the antenna can be used in more widespread application, especially in some harsh environment.

articleTitle: Design of Stand-Alone Photovoltaic System Based on Maximum Power Point Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a stand-alone photovoltaic power generation system with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and intelligent charging and discharging. The system uses single ended primary inductor converter(SEPIC) chopper circuit to form the direct current-direct current (DC-DC) module. Then the system uses MPPT algorithm with a combination of constant voltage tracking and perturbation and observation to automatically adjust the DC-DC module working state, so that the output power of photovoltaic cells approaches the maximum power point. The system uses segmented charging methods which include the maximum power point tracking charging method, constant current charging method, constant voltage charging method and floating charge method. By testing the system, the system can improve the efficiency of the photovoltaic cells by about 25%. The system can run stably and reliably.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Interference Coexistence in Dense Urban Scenario for 5G NR System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the advancing standardization of 5G systems, the study on interference coexistence problem in 5G system is becoming more and more crucial both in industry and academic. Moreover, the analysis method and simulation parameters for 5G new radio (NR) system are significantly different from those in mature LTE system due to the wider bandwidth and higher frequency. Thus it is necessary and urgent to study the interference coexistence issue in 5G system. In this paper, we analyze the coexistence problem of two 5G NR systems in dense urban scenario. Specifically, we consider the random drop network deployment that is selected in the 5G standardization, and the Manhattan network deployment which is more similar to the dense urban scenario. Moreover, the simulation model consists of propagation model, power control, beamforming, and link level performance model. To investigate the intra-system and inter-system interference, we utilize the Monte Carlo static snapshot approach and apply system level simulation. According to the simulation results, we get the necessary Adjacent Channel Interference Power Ratio (ACIR) between two 5G NR systems.

articleTitle: A Fast TDOA Estimation Algorithm for UAV Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The time difference of arrival (TDOA) is a key parameter of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) detection and location. The accuracy of TDOA estimation directly affects the positioning and tracking performance of UAV. In this paper, a fast and fine TDOA estimation algorithm based on Fourier transform (FFT) and quadratic interpolation is proposed for the commonly used orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technology in UAV. The algorithm firstly obtains the cross-power spectrum of two received signals. And crosscorrelation function is obtained by inverse Fourier transform of cross power spectrum. Compared with the traditional crosscorrelation function, the computational cost of this algorithm is less. Secondly, take the time difference corresponding to the maximum value of the cross-correlation function based on FFT as the initial value, and finally use quadratic interpolation to improve the accuracy of TDOA. The simulation results show that both the estimation accuracy and the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm are superior.

articleTitle: A Slow Rate Denial-of-Service Attack Against HTTP/2
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: HTTP/2 is the second major version of the HTTP protocol published by the IEIF. One of its purposes is to make more efficient use of the transmission efficiency of the TCP protocol. However, while improving efficiency, the emergence of the HTTP/2 protocol has also made attackers have another option to attack Web servers. This paper proposes a slow denial-of-service attack named zAttack against the HTTP/2 protocol, which sends specific request packets through a malicious client to cause the server to wait, continuously consume server resources and finally cause a denial-of-service attack. This paper uses a number of popular web servers to test this attack. The test results show that mainstream web servers that support the HTTP/2 protocol are vulnerable to this attack.

articleTitle: Vulnerability of Complex Networks under Neighbor Nodes Attack Strategies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Currently, for the reason that so multiple measures were deployed to protect the node of the max degree or betweenness, it was difficult to launch the traditional attack strategy which was initiated to destroy the nodes of the max degree or betweenness. As a result, the neighbor nodes of the max degree/betweenness node were become the first nodes to be destroyed by attacker because the protective measures on these neighbor nodes were generally relatively weak. In view of this, two neighbor nodes attack strategies of NND and NNB were proposed. The vulnerability of some complex networks was analyzed including three model networks (Random, Scale-free and Small-world) as well as four real networks (Word adjacencies, NetSience, Polblogs and Football) by using iterative execution. The results of experiment to three model networks and four real networks showed that the NND and NNB attack strategies almost had the same destructiveness to each of these three model networks, but under the same attack strategy, the model networks demonstrated that Scale-free network was the most vulnerable, while Small-world network was the best robustness.

articleTitle: Power Allocation for NOMA Based Layered Multicast Transmission
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), as a promising technology in 5G, can effectively improve the spectrum efficiency and user speed. The performance of multicast services in mobile communication networks is limited by the rate of the worst user, while NOMA can improve the quality of services for optimal channel users while guaranteeing the rate of the worst user of multicast group through power domain reuse. We focus on power allocation algorithms for NOMA based layered multicast transmission in this paper, with the purpose of maximizing sum rate in multicast system while giving attention to user fairness under the constraint of minimum rate and total transmit power. Based on layered multicast scene, a corresponding joint optimization algorithm for user group formation and power allocation is proposed. The effects of noise, user channel gain and power ratio on system performance were analyzed by means of theoretical analysis and simulation. Simulation results show that this algorithm further improves the sum rate of the system.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band and Dual-Circularly-Polarized Array Antenna with a Single Element
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A dual-band and dual-circularly-polarized (CP) array antenna is presented to achieve the wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidths. The TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01 </sub>modes of a dual-fed linearly polarized element are used to obtain the dual-frequency simultaneously. Sequential rotation technique with proper phase arrangement is used to achieve the dual-CP radiations. This antenna can radiate with left hand circular polarization (LHCP) in the lower band and right hand circular polarization (RHCP) in the higher band at the same time. Due to the single element on a single-layer substrate, the array antenna can be fabricated easily with less cost. This antenna has been investigated numerically and experimentally. Simulated results show that the -10-dB return loss bandwidths are 21.0% (8.6-10.6 GHz) and 12.5% (11.2-12.7 GHz) in the lower band centered at 9.5 GHz and higher band centered at 12 GHz, respectively. The 3-dB AR bandwidths in the low- and high-band are 8.4% (8.8-9.6 GHz) and 7.5% (11.8-12.7 GHz) respectively.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Malicious Punishment over Secure Distributed Estimation under Attacks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive malicious punishment DLMS algorithm to mitigate the adversarial attack. Two types of attacks are proposed in the WSNs. The adaptive threshold is designed to detect attacks. Then corresponding weight of malicious nodes can be reduced, due to the punishing factor. The simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is robust to the adversarial attacks.

articleTitle: Cooperative Beamforming for UAV-Assisted Cognitive Relay Networks with Partial Channel State Information
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a cooperative beamforming (BF) scheme for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted relay networks, where multiple UAVs are deployed as cognitive relays to assist the signal transmission between a cognitive transmitter and a cognitive receiver. Specifically, assuming that only the partial channel state information of each link is available, we first formulate an optimization problem to minimize the total transmit power of UAV relays under the constraints of the quality-of-service (QoS) requirement of the cognitive network and the interference limitation of the primary network. Then, a vector iterative algorithm is presented to solve the optimization problem so that the optimal BF weight vector is obtained. Finally, simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed BF algorithm and show the effects of UAV number and power constraint on the considered UAV-assisted network.

articleTitle: Phase Noise Compensation for DFT-s-OFDM Waveforms in MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Discrete Fourier Transform-spread Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (DFT-s-OFDM) features lower peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) than OFDM, with substantial benefits in terms of power efficiency. However, as it is susceptible to phase noise, a slight phase rotation may cause great reduction of system performance. In this paper, we focus on channel estimation stage and formulate a phase tracking reference signal (PTRS) assisted solutions for phase noise compensation for DFT-s-OFDM waveforms in MIMO system. In order to reduce overhead, we allow PTRS shares the same precoder as the antenna port (AP) of demodulation reference signal (DMRS) with the strongest signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). PTRS inserted in both time domain and frequency domain are also devised to track the phase shift. Numerical simulation results corroborate the feasibility of the proposed precoding scheme, as it alleviates the effect of phase noise and achieves excellent error performance. Further more, both PTRS insertion schemes are able to provide substantially improved throughput of system.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation in Security Assurance
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Quantitative evaluation of system components, security assurance cases and system architecture are independently developed by using traditional approaches. This paper proposes a new approach which is possible to develop quantitative evaluation, security assurance and system architecture in an integrated way by using ArchiMate. This method can reduce the cognitive and operational gaps caused by operating and understanding different diagrams. The effectiveness of this method is also proved by comparative experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Co-frequency Interference of CBTC Signal Based on IEEE 802.11
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Communication-based train control (CBTC) systems adopt the wireless local area networks (WLAN) technology based on IEEE 802.11 protocol. The popularity of WiFi and other devices makes the 2.4 GHz co-frequency interference problem CBTC faced worse. In this paper, the reasons causing the CBTC systems to break in an emergency are analyzed: The co-frequency interference is too strong for the receivers to work properly; multiple users cause the CBTC signal's failure to access the channel or descending in performance of the receiver. Furthermore, field data test was designed and carried out on the subway line. After troubleshooting by analyzing the relevant parameters such as the number of packets, throughput, signal strength, etc., we find the amount of users requesting to connect to the Access Point (AP) “EN” during rush hours is extremely high, which results in more heavy co-frequency interference and degradation in performance of the receiver. Regarding this serious situation, we propose improvement methods to guarantee the normal operation of CBTC systems.

articleTitle: Joint TOA and DOA Estimation Based on Improved Matrix Pencil Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A single snapshot data can only provide less information so that subspace-class positioning parameters estimation algorithms depending on the covariance matrix fail. Aiming at solving this problem, a joint TOA (time of arrival) and DOA (direction of arrival) estimation based on improved matrix pencil method in wireless positioning is proposed. Firstly, according to the channel frequency domain response vector on the received array element, the data matrix containing delay and angle parameter information is obtained, then using the improved two-dimensional matrix pencil algorithm is to estimate the time delay parameter, then the direction of arrival parameter of the target signal is calculated by the relationship between the eigenvectors, so the joint estimation of two-dimensional parameters is accomplished. The algorithm avoids peak searching and parameter pairing search procedure, and it can obtain better parameter estimation performance with significantly reduced computational complexity. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A New Distributed Coalition Formation Algorithm for Cooperation in Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Stimulating cooperation among selfish nodes is critical to enhance network performance. In this paper, we formulate this problem as a coalition game formation among the rational nodes due to its features of ad hoc networks, instead of overlapping coalition formation game. In the game, each node can freely decide to choose a cooperative coalition for its incentive cooperation. Then, we devise a new and simple distributed coalition formation algorithm using the joining and leaving rules for each node's choice, so as to assure that the newly formed coalitional structure can converge to a stable structure. At last, we also verify the performance of the proposed algorithm through simulations, and compare it with the non-cooperative scheme. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has a better performance than the non-cooperative scheme.

articleTitle: Enabling Multiview- and Light Field-Video for Veridical Visual Experiences
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the advent of UHDTV and the inclusion of High Dynamic Range, High Frame Rate and Extended Color Gamut 2D-imagery is able to push technical parameters up to the limits of the human visual sense. Consequently, developments in sensor technology can be used to capture information beyond 2D-imagery. In this paper we introduce multiview- and light field-video as an option to capture (at least parts of) the plenoptic function and therewith drive veridical visual experiences. Our contribution is on tools for capturing and encoding so called 5D light fields. We have built a multi-camera array producing up to 6 GigaRays/s and a real-time hierarchical H.264 MVC encoder that enables encoding the light fields in form of a legacy compliant video stream.

articleTitle: Uplink User Power Control for Low-Orbit Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: For the low-orbit satellite uplink, the signal is affected by free space loss, rain attenuation, channel multipath fading, etc. during transmission. The user signal level received by the low-orbit satellite has large fluctuations, which affects the signal receiving performance. Therefore, the power control of the uplink user does not only need to compensate for the path loss and fading of the channel to ensure the establishment of the link, but also needs to reduce the power loss while satisfying the normal communication quality. The power control scheme proposed in this paper not only ensures the communication quality, but also improves the power utilization and stabilizes the received signal.

articleTitle: Analyses of Time Efficiency and Speed-ups in Inference Process of Two-Stage Object Detection Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the good performance of the two-stage object detection algorithms in accuracy, based on a typical two-stage method-Faster RCNN, this paper combs its framework, analyzes the time consumption and proposes four speed-ups-reducing the network layers, reducing the neurons, inputting multi-scale image and setting score threshold before sorting to reduce the computational complexity. Using the same PASCAL VOC 2007 datasets, the speed-ups proposed in this paper can improve the detection speed by 35% while keeping high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Improving Comprehensive Sampling Sets Matting Using Texture Feature
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Digital matting refers to the precise separation of the foreground from the background of image or video. It is a key technology in the fields of image processing and video editing which has a very broad application prospect. In this paper, we improve the two most important problems to be solved in the sampling based matting algorithms-how to handle unknown pixels that fail to acquire foreground and background pixel samples and how to process the color distribution overlapped regions of the foreground and the background pixels. By adding the LBP texture cost function to the CSS algorithm, a more comprehensive and representative samples are extracted, and then we can select the best foreground and background samples from them. The experimental results show that the algorithm in this paper is more comprehensive in sample collection, and the result of matting is more accurate.

articleTitle: Accelerometer-based Gesture Recognition Using MFCC and HMM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, an accelerometer-based gesture recognition system for mobile devices interaction has been proposed. A new feature extraction method for gesture recognition based on Mel Frequency Cepstrum Coefficient (MFCC) has been put forward. Since the accelerometer signals are sensitive to device's rotation, firstly a resultant force of acceleration is obtained and then their MFCCs are extracted as features. The Classifier used is Hidden Markov Model(HMM). An important problem is how to choose initial estimates of the HMM parameters. In our work, the segmental k-means segmentation with clustering method is adopted to estimate initial model parameters. The average recognition result of twenty complex gestures using the proposed method is effective. The experimental results show that gesture-based interaction can be used as a novel human computer interaction for consumer electronics and mobile devices.

articleTitle: Optimization of IMU Indoor Localization with Wireless Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents the development process of a wireless inertial measurement unit (IMU). A wireless communication configuration is designed for this unit. Low cost micro-electro-mechanical-systems (MEMS) accelerometers are used in the hardware prototyping.

articleTitle: A Physical-Layer Message Encryption and Authentication Scheme
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Most of physical-layer authentication schemes cannot prevent passive eavesdropping. In this paper, we propose a message encryption and authentication scheme based on physical-layer characteristics of wireless channel. By extracting the channel characteristics, the physical-layer key is generated. Then a key stream generator generates the key stream to protect the privacy of the transmitted data through the seed generated by a physical-layer key and an identity key. Finally, receiver authenticated the authenticity and integrity of the received message through a CRC check. Simulation results show that this scheme has a better performance in preventing both passive eavesdropping and active attack, thus the randomness of key stream is greatly improved and the rate of authentication missed detection rate is reduced by half.

articleTitle: Broadband Miniaturized Bandpass Frequency Selective Surfaces Based on Fractal Transmissive Metasurface Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, two kinds of broadband miniaturized bandpass frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) based on fractal transmissive metasurface elements at X band are proposed. FSSs satisfy butterworth response type and stack structures are used to expand bandwidth. FSSs are designed based on the concept of antenna-filter-antenna (AFA) which is employing fractal geometries for patches combined back-to-back and a cross-shaped slot or a double cross-shaped slot etched on the common ground plane with the unit-cell dimension and periodicity of 4.5mm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.15\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{0}$</tex>). The AFA-based FSSs exhibit superior frequency selectivity and have lower profile than conventional FSSs with an overall thickness of 2mm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.067\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{0}$</tex>) and 3mm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{0}$</tex>) respectively. Prototypes of the proposed FSSs are designed and simulated. To facilitate the design of this structure, a simple equivalent circuit is also presented in this paper. Presented FSSs demonstrate fractional bandwidths of 40% from 8GHz to 12GHz and 64% from 6.8GHz to 13.2GHz, which are corresponding to 3dB bandwidth of 4GHz and 6.4GHz respectively for both reflection (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) and transmission coefficients (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) at an incident angle within 60°. Compared to traditional FSSs, the designed FSSs are extremely useful in microwave wireless communication applications with a higher oblique incidence angle across wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: Balancing Energy Consumption Algorithm Based-on Controller Handover for Software-Defined Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, SDWSNs has been gaining more and more attention in the wireless sensor networks (WSNs) space. This phenomenon is mainly attributed to that both data collection and definable control can be more clearly achieved. However, simultaneously, there are some defects in energy balance and energy efficiency in SDWSNs, especially in the case of all nodes with limited energy. Large amounts of data reception will cause the rapid energy consumption in the aspect of energy of the controller, which will quickly lead to network failure. In this paper, to balance energy consumption of network in which energy of all nodes are limited and prolong lifetime of the network, we propose a novel balancing energy consumption algorithm based-on controller handover. In proposed algorithm, BP neural network is applied to support the mechanism of handover. Simulation results show that this algorithm can effectively balance energy consumption and extend lifetime of the network compared with the traditional energy saving algorithms in SDWSNs.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional Speaker Information Recognition with Multi-task Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to simultaneously estimate speaker identity and the other two traits of the speaker, specifically, emotion and gender. This simultaneous process is named as multi-dimensional speaker information recognition. We choose i-vector to represent the utterance with different duration as fixed length vector. In our paper, we first build individual neural networks (NN) for each single recognition task. In this single task, the input is i-vector of one speaker and the output is the corresponding one-hot vector. We then design a multi-task learning (MTL), the difference with the single task is the NN output, which contains three parallel one-hot vectors for MTL. The one-hot vectors denote the identity, emotion and gender information, respectively. The proposed approach is conducted on the KSU-Emotions corpus, which was recorded mainly for emotional recognition. Experimental results show that the best multi-task mechanism recognition accuracy is 4.6% better than the single task.

articleTitle: Sparse-Domain Interference Coordination Scheme in Ultra-Dense Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In ultra-dense networks, the amount of accessed devices is enormous, so the time costs of traditional inter-cell interference coordination (ICIC) schemes become drastically large, making them unusable anymore. In this paper, a sparse-domain ICIC scheme using wavelet transform is designed. Devices in each cell are first grouped and sorted to reveal the redundancy of the devices' useful signal and interference parameters. The parameters are then transformed to sparse domain by discrete wavelet transform and shortened by retaining only the scaling coefficients. In the end, ICIC is done in sparse domain and the obtained coordination strategy is transformed back to primitive domain by discrete wavelet inverse transform. Extensive simulations show that, compared with the traditional scheme achieving the optimal coordination, the proposed scheme dramatically reduces the time cost while keeping other metrics still close to the optima.

articleTitle: A Novel Comprehensive Quality Index QoX and the Corresponding Context-aware System Framework
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Context-aware systems are becoming increasingly popular and are widely used in many areas such as smart healthcare, digital home, and so on. The existing context-aware system frameworks mainly focus on the improvement of organization mode of the system modules, but they normally lack a quantitative and comprehensive quality index to describe and evaluate the overall system performance. In this paper, QoX is innovatively defined as a comprehensive quality index that combines quality of device (QoD), quality of context (QoC), quality of service (QoS) and quality of experience (QoE). Meanwhile, QoX is integrated into the context-aware system and a context-aware system framework based on QoX is proposed, which provides an effective model for rational use of context and optimal system design. Besides, by studying the relation among QoX related indicators, systems can actively adjust various preset thresholds and rules according to the changes of users' needs and environmental conditions, which would make systems more reliable and adaptive and provide users with personalized and intelligent services.

articleTitle: An Improvement of the Remote Authentication Scheme for Anonymous Users Using an Elliptic Curve Cryptosystem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: It is convenient to obtain the information resources via intelligent devices over cloud systems. The user authentication mechanism is a fundamental tool for ensuring the validity of communicating parties and securing communications among the communicating party. Recently, Zhang et al. proposed a new remote authentication scheme for anonymous users using an elliptic curve cryptosystem. Their scheme could achieve the mutual authentication and forward security. They claimed that their scheme could withstand various attacks by employing BAN-logic formal methods. They claimed that their scheme could withstand the preserving anonymity and non-traceability, perfect forward secrecy, offline password guessing attacks, forgery attacks, server impersonating attacks, known key attacks, and reply attacks. However, we will show that their scheme is vulnerable to forgery attacks, server impersonating attacks, and man-in-the-middle attacks. In this article, we also propose an improved anonymous user authentication scheme proposed by Zhang et al. to withstand the vulnerability in their scheme.

articleTitle: An Opportunistic Routing Protocol based on Link Quality and Local Topology in Mobile Ad hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs), the frequent changes of network topology due to node mobility increases the cost of maintaining deterministic routing. As one state-less routing protocol, opportunistic routing utilizes the nature of broadcast and does not have to maintain deterministic routes. However, broadcast may cause interference to some nodes and affect the transmission quality between nodes. Thus, how to adapt opportunistic routing to the dynamic environment and avoid unreliable transmissions are two important issues to solve. In this paper, we propose an opportunistic routing protocol based on link quality and local topology (OR-LqT) in MANETs. In the protocol, we measure link qualities by considering both interference and nodes' mobility to find the candidate set, and select a next forwarding node by prioritizing the neighbor nodes based on their locations, local topology and moving adaptivity. The proposed OR-LqT can avoid the number of unreliable transmissions and the number of dead-ends. The performance results show that compared to the conventional routing protocols, such as AODV, PRR*d and GPSR, the OR-LqT decreases the number of dead-ends by more than 33.5%, packet drop ratio by more than 21%, average delay by more than 22% and overhead by more than 21%.

articleTitle: Analysis for Influence of Training Data Sequence on CNN-based Steganalysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recent studies have proved that CNN (Convolution neural network) is an effective method to solve steganalysis problem. In this paper, we analyze the influence of the input data sequence on CNN training results according to the training mechanism of CNN. The differences made by variant data sequence may be caused by data correlation, data mini-batch processing and high-pass filtering operations. In experiment, the accuracy of CNN detection with variant data sequence was compared, with cover and stego produced by two steganography algorithms (S_UNIWARD, WOW) with different embedding rates (0.1, 0.4). Results demonstrate that the network detection effect of pairwise data is better than that of random one.

articleTitle: Predicting Micro-blog Individual Retweet Behavior Based on User's Interest Drift
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Micro-blog post retweet prediction is one of the key technologies for researching information dissemination. The factors that affect retweet are multifaceted; However, the existing methods mainly focus on the research of micro-blog post information attributes and network structure characteristics, and do not fully consider the interests of users that are changing with time. To address this issue, we firstly propose some new methods of measuring features, which are user's influence, user's intimacy with named entities and users' intimacy. Meanwhile, in order to solve this problem of user' s interest changing, we propose a topic model based on user's interest drift to measure user's current interest and calculate topic similarity between users. Finally, we establish a novel micro-blog prediction retweet model based on above features. Our experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method has superior accuracy and stability, compared with several classification methods.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Metaheuristic Optimization of Gradients as an Alternative to Backpropagation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we continue our research on the previously proposed “favorable gradients”, the gradients selected by random search that are beneficial for training of DNNs. The contribution of this study can be stated as follows: we experimentally analyze two methods of calculating gradients - backpropagation and favorable gradients optimization - and we show that the gradients can be optimized by metaheuristic optimization techniques such as evolution strategies and further used for training DNNs with a selected optimizer. Thus, the proposed method can be viewed as an alternative to backpropagation, since it is theoretically possible to train DNNs end-to-end by using only favorable gradients. However, in practice this method turns out to be considerably slower than backpropagation, therefore a combination of these two techniques has been examined.

articleTitle: DGPA-Based Tone Reservation for PAPR Reduction in OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we concentrate on the high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction issue in the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system based on the tone reservation (TR) method. We first apply the discrete generalized pursuit algorithm (DGPA) to search the optimal peak reduction tone (PRT) set. Then, we compare the performance and computational complexity (CC) between the DGPA and other techniques in finding the PRT set. Furthermore, we apply the PRT set searched by the DGPA in the TR method to reduce the high PAPR. And we compare the PAPR reduction and the bit error rate (BER) performance between three methods. Finally, the simulation results verify that the proposed method in this paper can achieve the similar BER performance as the other benchmarks but have better performance in PAPR reduction.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation for IoT Devices in FeD2D Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Compared to the conventional human-to-human devices, the Internet of Things (IoT) devices needs fewer resources and lower power for data transmissions. As a result, how to increase the resource utilization efficiency and energy efficiency simultaneously is worth studying while enabling different types of IoT devices access to the future 5G networks. In this paper, we study a distance-based algorithm for resource allocation in a Further Enhancement to Device-to-Device (FeD2D) network. Firstly, an appropriate distance for resource reuse is found out to decrease the co-channel interference (CCI) between different relay user equipments (UEs). Then, more direct communications are processed in one subframe to improve the energy and resource utilization efficiencies in the proposed algorithm based on reuse condition. Simulation results verify the advantage of the proposed algorithm in power saving and full use of resources.
