articleTitle: On Six Directions Chain Code and Its Application of Bead Weaving
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a new six directions chain code based on the classical Freeman code. It can be applied to graphics that involves hexagonal cells or boundaries. Compare to 8 directions chain code, 6 directions chain code is distortion-free under rotations. This paper also discusses the weaving path problem in bead weaving especially for the ring bead cushion using 6 directions chain code. According to the description of the periodicity and regularity of the weaving path, the algorithm flow chart is provided. Computer simulation shows that 6 directions chain code can precisely picture the path of bead weaving. The main contribution of this paper are to create a new application field of six directions chain code and provide the theoretical basis for designing and manufacturing a bead weaving machine.

articleTitle: Error Elimination Method for TOA Based Wireless Cooperative Localization Networks in NLOS Case
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the problems of locating the target and reducing the errors in three-dimensional (3D) wireless cooperative localization networks, utilizing time of arrival (TOA) in the presence of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) error and clock jitter error. Through linearizing the range-based expressions and utilizing novel three-step weighted linear least squares (T-SWLLS) algorithm, a closed solution of target position can be obtained, in which errors can be reduced effectively. Meanwhile, the simulation results indicate that the precision of the proposed algorithm can close to Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB), the presented approach is obviously superior to the traditional algorithms in positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: Distant Supervision for Relation Extraction via Retrieval-based Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Relation Extraction is an important task in natural language processing (NLP) and Knowledge Base (KB) constructing. Distant Supervision (DS) is a widely used technique for automatically labeling training data by aligning the triples in a KB with free text. However, most methods treat DS relational extraction as a classification problem, which are vulnerable to dataset distribution. In this paper, we propose a retrieval-based method based on piecewise convolutional neural networks (called RPCNN) for DS relation extraction, which calculate relation retrieval scores between input features and relation features before classification. We apply knowledge embedding learning model to learn relation feature vectors from the KB used in DS, which means that our model could leverage the semantic knowledge in the KB to improve the relation extraction. Experimental results on widely used datasets show that our RPCNN model outperform all the baseline systems.

articleTitle: The Attack Surface Shifting in the Mimic Defense System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The notion of attack surface shifting is introduced to describe the situation of shifting the attack surface in the moving target defense system. However, the situation of shifting the attack surface in the mimic defense system is different from the situation of shifting the attack surface in the moving target defense system. Hence, the existing notion of attack surface shifting can't be applied to describe the situation of shifting the attack surface in mimic defense system. In this paper, we redefine the notion of attack surface shifting for the mimic defense system, and provide a formal method for quantifying the shifting. Experimental results reveal that the new notion of attack surface shifting contributes to improve the strategy of scheduling the heterogeneous redundant executive entity so as to enhance the security of mimic defense system.

articleTitle: Passive Positioning for LTE User Equipment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel positioning algorithm for LTE user equipment (UE), which utilizes the random access procedure. Unlike the observed time different of arrival (OTDOA) algorithm first proposed in 3GPP technical specification Release 9, the novel algorithm neither needs the positioning reference signals nor multi-eNodeBs, the positioning cost of which is greatly reduced on the premise of high precision. The algorithm can be a beneficial addition to indoor positioning for UE with poor positioning reference signals in indoor environment. Further, it can also be used for user information collection in the region of interest by relevant government departments. Compared with the notorious IMSI-catcher, the characteristic of passive reception makes this algorithm never impact the normal communication behavior.

articleTitle: Analyzing Core Structure and Role Transition Features of Terrorist Organizations Based on Meta-Network Take Al Qaida as an Example
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of global counter-terrorism, the structure of terrorist organizations has gradually changed from the traditional hierarchy to the covert network, equipping them with stronger survivability and higher attack efficiency. In recent years, a significant amount of research on terrorist incidents has been conducted worldwide by using social network analysis, which effectively revealed the structural features of terrorist organizations and helped people understand the law of their formation and activity. In this paper, we first build a meta-network model for Al Qaida and discover that the structure of Al Qaida is a cellular network composed of multiple units. Second, terrorist events are clustered by using K-means algorithm to identify the role distribution characteristics in the organization. Results reveal that logistical personnel account for a large portion of each task. Third, the role transition network is constructed by calculating the connectivity matrix, which indicates that obvious hierarchical phenomenon exists in the role transition of Al Qaida. Finally, key members in Al Qaeda are recognized by using multivariate capacity index, which is more accurate than the traditional network analysis method.

articleTitle: Sentiment-Polarized Word Embedding for Multi-label Sentiment Classification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of text is an import branch of natural language process. In this paper, we propose a sentiment-polarized word embedding model (SPWE) with emotional dictionary, which is a variant of the C&W. Our model is able to represent and differentiate the emotional semantic of words, which is critical in sentiment classification tasks. This weak supervised model can perform large scale corpus training just with an open source emotional dictionary. In addition, we optimize the objective function from our previous hierarchical model and propose a Relax Margin loss function. The result shows it can reduce overfitting and improve generalization ability by restricting approximation degree to probability distribution of the multi-labels. We release our manually labeled comment dataset with multi tags from our previous work, and our code is available in https://github.com/KillersDeath/SPWE.

articleTitle: Interference-based VM Migration to Mitgate Cache-based Side-channel Attacks in Cloud
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Co-residency of different clients' VMs on the same hardware platform puts users at risk of cache-based side-channel attacks in cloud. While current countermeasures fail to be general and precise, we observe that cache behaviors of co-resident VMs interfere with each other. So we set up a novel cache interference model which precisely depicts how a bystander's behavior affects cache side channels between VMs. Based on this model, we propose an interference-based VM migration strategy to defend against cache attacks by co-locating multiple VMs so as to maximize the effect of one VM's cache activities on disrupting the cache access pattern of another VM which might be utilized by side-channel attackers. Simulation result shows that our approach is effective against cache attacks by improving the average interference ratio by about 35%.

articleTitle: Study on A-Pillar Display Algorithm through Image Registration
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, A-pillar display algorithm with robustness is studied in the case of a fast-moving vehicle. For closed load-bearing structures of a car, A-pillar carries the body structure and the frontal impact pressure of the cockpit, so A-pillar plays an important role in improving the stability and rigidity of the car as well as safe driving. A-pillar is designed for dynamics considerations, however, some drawbacks exists, such as the binocular visual obstacle. The visual impairment caused by A-pillar affects safe driving and on the other hand, has the disadvantage of poor driving experience. To solve this problem, we implement A-pillar display through image registration for images that are captured simultaneously by two hand-held cameras. Through image registration, the blind area of A-pillar is detected and displayed from the driver's perspective.

articleTitle: Supervised Learning Method for Link Adaptation Algorithm in Coded MIMO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The traditional link adaptation scheme requires packet error rate based on channel state information (CSI). The adaptive selection of the modulation and coding schemes (MCS) is usually decided according to estimation of packet error rate. Unfortunately, the integration of channel coding, OFDM technology and multi-antenna technology in Multiple-Input, Multiple-Output-Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing(MIMOOFDM) wireless communication systems makes traditional prediction of packet error rate very complicated. This paper proposes a new framework based on supervised learning approach k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) algorithm for adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) in MIMO-OFDM wireless systems. With the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the channel matrix, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) on each spatial stream is extracted as a feature set. A classification scheme is then proposed to match channel implementations to different MCSs. The simulation results show that the proposed framework can successfully classify each MCS and perform perfect selection of MCS for frequency flat fading channels.

articleTitle: Multi-focus Image Fusion Framework Using Total Variation and Phase Congruency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-scale decomposition (MSD) strategy is wildly applied to extract characteristics at different scales in image fusion field, and then the different image components will stay in different layers. To avoid the negatively impact that using the same fusion rule on different scales, a Gaussian filter MSD-based of fusion method with total variation (TV) and phase congruency (PC) is proposed in this paper. This framework consists of three parts: First, decompose the source images into base layer and detail layer through Gaussian filter; Then, TV and PC are set as the representations of base and detail layers, respectively; Finally, combine the fusing two layers to reconstruct the fused image. Some fusion methods and several quantitative analyses are displayed, and the experimental results show that the proposed method has a superior performance compared with some other popular fusion methods, both in human vision and objective evaluations.

articleTitle: EHTC: An Enhanced Huffman Tree Coding Algorithm and its FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Many computer systems require storing a large volume of data sets, which are steadily increasing as computer applications are extended to new disciplines. Simultaneously, the proliferation of computer networks is resulting in a massive transfer of data over communication links. Consequently, reduction of transmitted data directly leads to an increased capacity of communication channels. This project aims to design and implement an Enhanced Huffman Tree Coding system that compresses the data by encoding it via a sorting table, which keeps track of compressed data by assigning characters with dedicated keywords. The proposed algorithm improves the speed of decoding operations based on the Variable Length Coding decoder-partitioning concept. The coding system is implemented using HDL language and Matlab and simulated on Altera Quartus16 for functional verification. The executed design is synthesized using Altera Cyclone FPGA.

articleTitle: Multimodal Biometric Authentication System for Smartphone Based on Face and Voice Using Matching Level Fusion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recently, the multimodal biometrics authentication method has been widely studied since it can overcome the deficiency of unimodal biometric. In this paper, a multimodal biometric authentication system for smartphone based on face and voice is developed to solve the problem where the single biometric is easy to be stolen. In view of the low CPU performance of the smartphone, which can't store and quickly process large amount of data, face detection is carried out after image acquisition and redundant background image is discarded to reduce futility information effectively. In addition, the traditional LBP operator is improved to enhance the robustness of the authentication system and the traditional endpoint detection technology is optimized to deal with the mute and transition information in the voice stream. For the authentication process, an adaptive fusion strategy based on the matching level is proposed. The simulation experiments based on PC show that the authentication accuracy of our algorithm on the benchmark database reaches 100% when the training sample number is 5, and the single authentication time is about 341ms. A lot of test experiments on smartphone show that our system achieves perfect authentication effect and meets the requirements in practical application.

articleTitle: Dynamic Computation and Radio Resource Allocation in Downlink Green C-RAN Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Cloud radio access network (C-RAN) is a promising solution for future wireless network due to easy cooperation among remote radio heads (RRHs) and concentrated management in baseband unit (BBU) pool. Physical servers in the BBU provides computation ability in the form of virtual machines(VMs) to manage data of different users. In this paper, we focus on a scenario where each server dynamically provides computation capability according to users'(UE) quality of service (QoS) requirement, which is more practical. By jointly optimizing joint beamforming, RRH selection and dynamic computation allocation under the constraint of limited fronthaul and computation capacity, we minimize the network power consumption (NPC) in both RRHs and BBU pool. The formulated problem is non-convex and difficult to solve in general. We propose a simple two-step iterative algorithm to solve the problem. Firstly, we solve the common wireless optimization problem without considering computation allocation. Then by fixing the transmitting beamforming, we solve the computation resource allocation problem, which is a 0-1 multiple knapsack problem (MKP). Simulation results suggests that our proposed dynamic resource allocation algorithm can improve the system performance and save energy.

articleTitle: An All-to-All Broadcast Algorithm with Variable Length Packets in Ad Hoc Networks Using Directional Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The all-to-all broadcast means that nodes can share their own packets to all the other nodes in the network. Most of researches on all-to-all broadcast with the TDMA (Time Division Multiple Access) mechanism are based on the fixed length packet model. But in practical scenarios, the packets have the different length according to their contents. Therefore, an all-to-all broadcast algorithm ABVP (An All-to-All Broadcast Protocol for Variable Packet Sizes) was proposed to tackle the variable length packets with a mechanism of eliminating redundant transmissions. However, ABVP leads to the idle resources. In order to solve the problem in ABVP, we propose a low latency solution for all-to-all broadcast of non-fixed length packet (ABNLP). The simulation results by network simulation software OPNET14.5 show that, compared with ABVP algorithm, ABNLP can reduce the all-to-all broadcast delay up to 48% and decrease average number of transmission times. As a result, the overall energy consumption of network is reduced.

articleTitle: Voice Intonation Transformation Using Segmental Linear Mapping of Pitch Contours
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Voice transformation converts the voice of a speaker to an intended person, such that the listener is deceived for the target speaker. Voice transformation has many application like low bandwidth speech encoding, voice disguise, entertainment, voice morphing. The proposed methodology transforms the pitch contour of one speaker to another by segmental linear mapping of the pitch contour. This method considers sound as an one-dimensional continuous signal. A linear mapping function is considered to transform pitch contour i.e. y(t) = f(x(t)), where y(t), x(t) are two different pitch contours of sound signal and f is the mapping function. The segmentation of the pitch contour is done using linguistically motivated parameters, which are extracted automatically from the audio signals to capture the inotation of the voice. The proposed methodology do not need any large speech corpus for training or learning the speech intonation generation, making the methodology computationally efficient. The simulation result proves the efficiency of the transformation of the pitch contour.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Particle Swarm Optimization Based Long Short-Term Memory Method for Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) is indispensable for human-machine interaction. Related applications in many fields, e.g. medical, military, and security, facilitate and even change the lives of human beings. However, a key issue, i.e. the unsatisfactory recognition accuracy, still remains to be addressed. In this paper, we explore a new way to design a long short-term memory (LSTM) method specifically for HAR with datasets collected by sensors or mobile devices. In particular, combining with the multidimensional particle swarm optimization (MD-PSO), the LSTM method, which has advantages in processing collected datasets with timing characteristics, is not only optimized in terms of parameters (i.e. weights and bias), but also of the network topology as well as the number of blocks in each layer. In other words, we can further get the optimal topology and network mapping parameters of the LSTM network under the conditions of supervised learning. By utilizing the real dataset, performance of the proposed method is verified. Moreover, the test results show that our method significantly outperforms the commonly used support vector machine (SVM) and LSTM methods.

articleTitle: Empirical Study on Web-Based Facial Recognition Services
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Face recognition as an identity authentication has been widely used in commodity mobile systems. However due to increasing attacks against face recognition algorithms, mobile systems users begin to concern about the security and reliability of face recognition modules in their mobile devices. In China, many commercial devices manufacturers prefer to adapt web-based API to their devices as the user authentication method. In this paper, we focus on accuracy and reliability performance in both Baidu and Face++ face comparison API. To make a comparison, we also tested on Google facenet as the baseline. The result shows that liveness detection method has not been widely applied in web based API. Those without liveness detection will be vulnerable to presentation attack. Depends on the security level, a certain mount of presentation attack could be prevented by current liveness detection method.

articleTitle: Topology Construction of Backbone Network Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a topology construction scheme of backbone network. In this scheme, topology construction is abstracted to classification problem in machine learning area. We select/extract features based on network science theory and basic models of topology construction. In the experiments, we collect data set from actual backbone topology in China, compare and analyse several machine learning algorithms and study the influence of different parameters on topology construction. Results show that the proposed scheme has ideal applicability: The similarity between actual topology and the topology built by the scheme exceeds 98%. The feature extraction process is concise and there is no need to deliberately screen the data set. Among the algorithms involved in this paper, the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) and Random Forest algorithm have the most ideal performance. Our study shows that the topology construction in backbone network, which is basically dominated by engineering experience and influenced by many different factors, can be well simulated by machine learning algorithms, providing new ideas for the innovation of backbone network planning.

Author Keywords: network planning network construction network science machine learning

articleTitle: Uplink Power Control of the DUDE Mode in HetNets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As current cellular networks are becoming increasingly heterogeneous, traditional cell association rule based on the maximum downlink received power no longer serves well. The downlink and uplink decoupling (DUDE) are proposed for improving system performance. However, in DUDE association scheme, macro user equipment (MUE) will suffer more interference from the offloaded DUDE user equipment (DUDE UE) in uplink. In this paper, we apply the power control scheme to mitigate co-channel interference from small user equipment (SUE) and DUDE UE to MUE and guarantee the Quality of Service (QoS) of each user. We extend three power control schemes in homogeneous networks to HetNets and compare the convergence and optimality of these schemes through theory analysis. In addition, we propose an improved distributed power control (IDPC) scheme. The simulation results show that the IDPC scheme can effectively improve the system performance, especially when many users suffering severe mutual interference.
